scope.purpose: separate fresh-boundary initialization drift from truncated fixed-point drift

method.fresh_probe: run the paired-gauged tensor from its deterministic boundary initialization
method.transported_probe: transport the resident solved environment with the explicit fused inverse-transpose edge map, then run the paired-gauged tensor from that environment
method.admission_rule: fresh paired-gauge validation remains the admission gate; transported probe is diagnostic-only

ghz_fixture.interpretation: transport removes the GHZ initialization-sector drift, but this does not establish covariance of a generic truncated fixed point

random_fixture.terms: onsite Z coefficient 1.0 and nearest-neighbor ZZ coefficient 1.0

cuda_fixture.terms: onsite Z coefficient 1.0 and nearest-neighbor ZZ coefficient 1.0
cuda_fixture.interpretation: transport lowers the CUDA drift but remains above the 1e-4 admission tolerance

conclusion: Resident-environment transport is algebraically useful and can remove a degenerate-sector initialization artifact, but generic random D=2 results remain above the declared 1e-4 gate. The unresolved problem is the covariant truncated fixed-point map, not merely fresh initialization.
resource_note: bounded CPU complex128 probe; no large sweep
